title: Reviews & blogs
examples: How do I make my opinion sound more convincing in a review?
What is the difference between my voice and the tone of a review?
Should I use too many adjectives when writing a blog?

explain.say: Today we are learning to write convincing reviews and blog posts.
First, you need a clear opinion about what you are reviewing.
Next, you must support that opinion with specific evidence from the work.

items: Evidence: The final scene showed the character overcoming fear.
Conclusion: This makes the book powerful.

explain.say: A strong voice means you sound like yourself writing the review.
For a real-life example, imagine reviewing a new local cafe.

items: Coffee | 4/5 | The latte art was perfect.
Seating | 3/5 | The chairs felt a little wobbly.

explain.say: The most common mistake is stating opinions without any proof.

items: Instead, say: 'The plot dragged during the middle chapters.'
This points to a specific part of the story.

faq.q: Should I use slang when writing a blog review?
faq.a: It depends on your intended audience. If you are writing for friends, casual slang is fine. If you are writing for a school assignment, it is best to keep your language standard.
asks: Is it okay to use emojis in a review?

faq.q: How many pieces of evidence should I include?
faq.a: You should include at least two or three pieces of specific evidence. This helps your reader believe your overall opinion.
asks: Do I need a lot of examples?

faq.q: Does my voice need to be consistent throughout?
faq.a: Yes, your voice should stay consistent. If you start sounding very formal, do not suddenly switch to being overly casual without a reason.
asks: Can I change my voice halfway through?

faq.q: Is it better to be positive or negative in a review?
faq.a: It is better to be honest, whether positive or negative. The key is to support your feeling with clear reasons.
asks: Should I only write good things?
Is it harder to write a bad review?

faq.q: What is the difference between tone and voice?
faq.a: Your voice is your natural style, like your handwriting. Your tone is the feeling you are giving right now, like being sarcastic or excited.
asks: Are tone and voice the same thing?
How do I change my tone?

facts: A review aims to give an evaluation of a product or work.
Opinion statements must always be backed up by specific evidence.
Your writing voice is the unique personality that comes through your words.
When writing for a blog, you can often use a more informal voice.

quiz.say: I think this movie was amazing because the special effects were breathtaking.

options.show: The phrase 'special effects were breathtaking' is the evidence.
options.say: The phrase 'special effects were breathtaking' is the evidence.

options.show: I think this movie was amazing.
options.say: I think this movie was amazing.

quiz.why: This answer correctly shows that the opinion ('amazing') is supported by a specific detail ('special effects').

wrong.1: This is only an opinion and lacks any supporting details.
wrong.2: This is too broad and does not tell the reader why you feel that way.
wrong.3: This is only a fact about the film, not a clear opinion about the whole work.

quiz.say: Which sentence shows a consistent, enthusiastic voice?

options.show: Wow, this book was absolutely incredible from start to finish!
options.say: Wow, this book was absolutely incredible from start to finish!

quiz.why: This sentence uses strong, excited language that keeps the reader engaged.

wrong.1: This is too simple and does not show any strong personality.
wrong.2: This is neutral and does not convey any clear voice or feeling.
wrong.3: This is just a factual statement about when you read it.

quiz.say: If I write a review for a science textbook, what should my voice generally be?

options.show: A formal and objective voice is best for textbooks.
options.say: A formal and objective voice is best for textbooks.

quiz.why: Academic reviews require measured language that focuses on content rather than personal excitement.

wrong.1: This is too emotional for a formal textbook review.
wrong.2: This is too informal and uses casual language.
wrong.3: This sounds like an advertisement rather than a thoughtful review.
